text:
rachel: Heads-up: Shinra v2.0-int8 onboarding smoke failed locale-mix (CJK+AR + emoji). sacreBLEU about -3.3 vs fp32 and we see broken grapheme clusters — emoji split and Arabic mirrored when adjacent to Han.

tom: yikes. quick repro?

rachel: minimal case from locale-mix-v4: payload: ```json {
  "src": "\u4eca\t\u5929\u3002 \u0627\u0628\u062c \uD83D\uDE0A",
  "lang": "zh-ar_mixed"
} ``` (handy: CJK sentence + Arabic word + smiling emoji)

yuko: what does the model return?

rachel: staging raw: "\u4eca\u5929\u3002\u0627\u200F\u0628\u062c \uD83D\uDE0A" — note 1) U+200F RLM inserted between arabic grapheme clusters and 2) emoji came back as surrogate pair split into two tokens with a stray NULL between them.

tom: split surrogate pair suggests tokenizer produced two tokens for the emoji, and quantized embedding remap may have inserted a placeholder for unknown subunit. Did tokenization on CPU vs int8 differ?

rachel: token dumps: fp32 tokens: ["\u4eca\u5929\u3002", "\u0627\u0628\u062c", "\uD83D\uDE0A"]
int8 tokens: ["\u4eca\u5929\u3002", "\u0627", "\u200F", "\u0628\u062c", "\u0000", "\uD83D", "\uDE0A"]

yuko: interesting: Arabic word split into two tokens with RLM inserted, and emoji split to two tokens with a 0x00 placeholder in middle. That placeholder is suspect.

tom: check the vocabulary remap table used in quant conversion (vocab_remap.json). We had a shrink step for int8 that collapses rare graphemes into an escape token 0x00; maybe the remap mistakenly flagged half of some surrogate pairs as rare due to a UTF-8 length bug.

yuko: I pulled the remap diff for the int8 conversion: commit b7d4c2 "shrink-vocab-fast" changed the UTF-8 iterator to treat codepoints > U+FFFF as surrogate sequences when reading with byte-level slicing. That would incorrectly split emoji during remap.

rachel: aha. so an implementation bug in shrink step, not runtime bidi. But why RLM appears?

tom: RLM likely added later by fast-bidi sanitizer when it sees adjacent scripts. It runs per-token in the detok path and if it detects an Arabic run boundary it adds U+200F. Because token boundaries shifted (emoji split, arabic split), sanitizer thought it needed to insert RLM. So root cause: remap split tokens -> sanitizer wrong context -> RLM insertion.

yuko: proposed fixes: (1) revert shrink-vocab-fast change and add proper UTF-8 codepoint iteration for remap, (2) make sanitizer operate on grapheme clusters instead of token boundaries (cheap guard: if token is a surrogate pair, treat as single).

rachel: prioritize (1) in onboarding pipeline; (2) is a runtime safety guard. Also add a unit test: mixed CJK+AR+emoji to locale-mix-v4.

dev-bot: created branch fix/shrink-utf8-codepoint-2891 and triggered CI/onboard/shinra-int8-smoke.

bench-bot: perf note: reverted shrink version increases model size by ~0.6% but latency unaffected.

tom: acceptable. can we patch staging quickly and re-run the smoke?

deploy-bot: deploy request queued eng-ml/staging -> fix/shrink-utf8-codepoint-2891 by rachel. ETA 10m.

yuko: also added sanitizer change to skip adding bidi markers when prev/next tokens include non-splittable grapheme (is_surrogate_pair(token) or contains_zwj). Unit tests added.

rachel: re-run local smoke: sacreBLEU diff now -0.05 vs fp32 ; emoji intact and no RLM.

tom: great catch. let's add this mixed-case to onboarding gates for int8/int6 and add a small doc note in model-onboard.md about utf8 iterator assumptions when remapping vocab.

yuko: done: PR #412 in infra/docs added. Also backport to other shrink-vocab branches.

rachel: leaving thread open until nightly locale-mix-v4 is green. thanks. :pray:

dev-bot: nightly locale-mix-v4 job queued. artifacts will appear in morning run.

bench-bot: monitoring: no regression in p50 observed post-fix.
